stories.title: Progress Kemp LoadMaster Flaw Hits CISA KEV After 792 Reported Exploit Attempts
stories.abstract: CISA has added a critical command injection vulnerability in Progress Kemp LoadMaster, tracked as CVE-2026-8037, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Unauthenticated attackers are actively leveraging this flaw to execute arbitrary code on affected systems.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows remote, unauthenticated code execution, posing a severe risk of full system compromise for exposed load balancing infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for Progress Kemp LoadMaster immediately.

stories.title: Dell security advisory (AV26-788)
stories.abstract: Multiple vendors have released security patches addressing various vulnerabilities. Affected products include Dell OpenManage Server Administrator, RVTools, Dell Virtual Storage Integrator, GitHub Enterprise Server, and Progress MarkLogic Server. One vulnerability, CVE-2026-63077, is currently listed on the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: The inclusion of a KEV-listed vulnerability indicates active exploitation, necessitating immediate attention to these specific infrastructure and development platform updates.
stories.action: Update Dell OpenManage, RVTools, VSI, GitHub Enterprise, and MarkLogic Server to the latest patched versions.

stories.title: Framework loses customer data in Metabase zero-day attack
stories.abstract: Framework Computer confirmed a data breach resulting from the exploitation of a critical SQL injection vulnerability in the Metabase business intelligence platform. Attackers leveraged this zero-day flaw to gain unauthorized access to customer information stored within the company's internal systems.
stories.why: Third-party analytics and BI tools often serve as high-value targets for attackers seeking to bypass perimeter defenses and access sensitive backend databases.

stories.title: Metabase Zero-Day Exploited in Wild Allows Admin Access Without Authentication
stories.abstract: Metabase has released a patch for a critical, unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability currently being exploited in the wild. The flaw allows attackers to inject arbitrary SQL commands, granting them full administrative control over affected business intelligence instances.
stories.why: This critical flaw provides attackers with complete administrative access, posing a severe risk of data exfiltration and total system compromise.
stories.action: Update Metabase instances to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: TrueConf Server Flaws Exploited to Replace Client Installers with PhantomCore
Valve notifies Steam hardware customers of a data breach
stories.abstract: Valve notified European customers that their personal information, including names, physical addresses, and contact details, was compromised following a security breach at their third-party logistics provider, CEVA Logistics.
stories.why: Supply chain compromises remain a significant vector for data theft, highlighting the risks associated with third-party vendor access to sensitive customer databases.

stories.title: Attackers pick Levi's pockets in social engineering attack
stories.abstract: Levi Strauss & Co. confirmed a data breach resulting from a targeted social engineering campaign. Attackers successfully manipulated three employees into granting unauthorized access to their workstations, allowing the intruders to exfiltrate sensitive corporate information.
stories.why: This incident highlights the persistent risk of human-centric attacks bypassing technical controls to access internal corporate environments.

stories.title: WebPros security advisory (AV26-790)
stories.abstract: A blind SQL injection vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-64636, affects Plesk Obsidian versions prior to 18.0.80.1 and 18.0.79.5. Attackers could potentially exploit this flaw to manipulate database queries.
stories.why: SQL injection vulnerabilities allow unauthorized database access, potentially leading to data exfiltration or administrative compromise of the hosting environment.
stories.action: Update Plesk Obsidian to version 18.0.80.1 or 18.0.79.5 immediately.

stories.title: China-linked hackers turning popular cybersecurity tool into ransomware launchpad, Microsoft warns
stories.abstract: Microsoft identified a China-based threat group weaponizing a critical security flaw in N-able software to deploy ransomware. The attackers are leveraging the remote monitoring and management tool to gain unauthorized access and facilitate malicious encryption across target networks.
stories.why: Compromised management tools provide attackers with administrative control over entire enterprise environments, enabling widespread ransomware deployment.
stories.action: Audit N-able installations for unauthorized activity and verify all software is updated to the latest vendor-provided version.

stories.title: IBM security advisory (AV26-789)
stories.abstract: IBM has released a security advisory covering vulnerabilities across a broad range of enterprise products, including Cloud Pak for Data, Maximo Application Suite, PowerVC, and various automation and management tools. Users should review the specific affected versions listed in the advisory.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical infrastructure and management software, potentially exposing enterprise environments to unauthorized access or service disruption.
stories.action: Review the IBM security advisory and apply the recommended patches for your specific product versions.

stories.title: ClickFix attack pushes macOS infostealer for crypto theft attacks
stories.abstract: A new Go-based malware targeting macOS users is actively exfiltrating cryptocurrency wallets, browser credentials, Keychain data, and cached authentication tokens. The threat is currently being distributed via ClickFix social engineering tactics.
stories.why: This malware demonstrates a sophisticated capability to bypass standard macOS protections to harvest high-value secrets and financial assets.

stories.title: Google security advisory (AV26-787)
stories.abstract: Google has released security updates for Chrome to address two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-18556 and CVE-2026-18577, both of which are currently being exploited in the wild and have been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing an immediate risk of compromise to unpatched Chrome installations.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 151.0.7922.109 or later immediately.

stories.title: New Passkey Attacks Can Recover Synced Private Keys or Bypass Phishing-Resistant MFA
stories.abstract: Researchers identified three methods to circumvent passkey security by exploiting Windows authentication material, abusing cloud-synced credential systems, and leveraging malware already present on a host. These techniques bypass phishing-resistant MFA without needing to compromise the underlying cryptographic protocols.
stories.why: These findings highlight that passkeys are not immune to local system compromise or architectural flaws in how operating systems handle authentication tokens.

stories.title: Corporate Data Stolen in Levi Strauss Cyberattack
stories.abstract: Levi Strauss confirmed a security breach where attackers utilized social engineering tactics to compromise three employee workstations. The unauthorized parties successfully exfiltrated internal corporate data during the incident.
stories.why: This highlights the persistent effectiveness of social engineering in bypassing perimeter defenses to gain direct access to internal systems and sensitive data.

stories.title: When Credentials Are No Longer Enough: Device Trust in the AI Era
stories.abstract: Advancements in artificial intelligence are significantly enhancing the efficacy of phishing and credential harvesting. As traditional authentication methods like passwords and standard MFA become increasingly susceptible to bypass, organizations are shifting toward device-based trust signals to bolster their Zero Trust security architectures.
stories.why: Standard identity-based defenses are failing against AI-driven attacks, necessitating a move toward verifying device health and posture as a primary security control.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Monday, August 10th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10044, (Mon, Aug 10th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center's latest daily brief provides a summary of current cybersecurity trends and notable activity observed across the threat landscape for August 10th, 2026.
stories.why: Staying informed on daily threat telemetry helps security professionals identify emerging patterns and adjust defensive postures against active campaigns.

stories.title: CISA Flags TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation in the Wild
stories.abstract: CISA has added a critical deserialization vulnerability in on-premise JetBrains TeamCity instances to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-63077, allows unauthenticated remote code execution, and threat actors are currently leveraging it in active attacks.
stories.why: TeamCity servers are high-value targets for supply chain attacks, as they hold credentials and provide access to build pipelines and source code.
stories.action: Update on-premise TeamCity installations to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Cisco Warns of High-Severity ClamAV Vulnerabilities With Public PoC
stories.abstract: Cisco has disclosed high-severity vulnerabilities within the ClamAV antivirus engine. These flaws allow unauthenticated remote attackers to trigger denial-of-service conditions, and public proof-of-concept exploit code is currently available for the affected software.
stories.why: Publicly available exploit code increases the risk of service disruption for systems relying on ClamAV for threat detection and file scanning.
stories.action: Update ClamAV to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Shipping 10–50× More Code? Watch This Webinar on Securing AI-Speed Development
stories.abstract: The rapid adoption of AI-assisted coding tools is significantly increasing software output, creating a disconnect between development velocity and traditional security review processes. Organizations now face challenges in maintaining oversight and vulnerability management as code volume scales exponentially.
stories.why: Accelerated development cycles can outpace security controls, leading to unvetted dependencies and increased risk exposure in production environments.

stories.title: New Jersey, Alabama Join States Targeted in Water Cyberattacks
stories.abstract: Iranian-affiliated threat actors are actively targeting industrial control systems within water infrastructure across multiple U.S. states. Recent reports confirm that facilities in New Jersey and Alabama have been added to the growing list of compromised or targeted entities.
stories.why: Critical infrastructure remains a primary target for state-sponsored actors, highlighting significant vulnerabilities in operational technology environments that lack robust perimeter security.

stories.title: New Zealand sanctions Russian hackers, propaganda groups over Ukraine war
stories.abstract: New Zealand has imposed fresh sanctions targeting Russian technology firms, state-aligned propaganda entities, and cyber threat actors. These measures aim to disrupt organizations providing material or digital support to the ongoing military campaign in Ukraine.
stories.why: These sanctions signal increased international pressure on Russian cyber assets, potentially impacting the operational capabilities of state-sponsored hacking groups.

stories.title: Snowflake Hacker Pleads Guilty Over Breaches Affecting at Least 100 Million People
stories.abstract: Connor Riley Moucka, a Canadian national, has pleaded guilty to orchestrating a massive campaign that compromised over 165 Snowflake customer environments. The operation resulted in significant data theft, including millions of AT&T customer records, and yielded over $2.5 million in extortion payments.
stories.why: This case highlights the severe risks of credential stuffing and inadequate MFA implementation in cloud environments, leading to widespread enterprise data breaches.
